_changelog: 2026-08-29 — Asian Base Block macros corrected. The file previously carried three independently hand-maintained figures (per-block macros, per-100g-cooked macros, batch yield) that contradicted each other by ~34%. The per-100g-cooked value of 105 kcal implied a cooked weight of ~1126 g, which is more than goes into the pot. Since MacroFactor logging uses grams, the wrong one of the two was in daily use. Ingredients now carry their own nutrition, cooked weight is a single declared field, and every macro below is DERIVED by scripts/recompute_macros.py. Do not edit the 'computed' blocks by hand.

2026-08-29 — energyFactors added so the kitchen page can check a meal target against its own arithmetic. First result: the mirror-meal spec overshoots its calorie budget by ~10 kcal at the theoretical floor, i.e. it is unreachable, not merely difficult. No recipe can satisfy it.

2026-08-29 — mirror meal raised to 470 kcal on 1 block with 14 g fibre, after a search over the kitchen's own staples showed the old 425/17/1.5 spec had a floor of 533 kcal. Block ladder halved to 0.5 / 1 / 1.5.

2026-08-30 — check_targets.py gained a REAL FOOD section. The block ladder prices macros at the Atwater floor, so its verdict was necessary and not sufficient; the new search constructs actual plates from foods.json and reports how many fit and which protein sources cannot. Result: the current spec is comfortable, the old one returns zero plates at 1, 1.5 and 2 blocks, and the binding constraint is the 12 g fat ceiling rather than the fibre.

yield._note: 425 g raw solids plus the water retained after the 5-10 min steam-off. This is the ONE number that must be measured. Weigh the next batch, put the real figure here, re-run scripts/recompute_macros.py — every macro in this file follows from it. An estimate that is 50 g off shifts kcal/100g by about 6%.

energyFactors._note: Atwater factors, kcal per gram. Present for one purpose: to check whether a meal target is arithmetically reachable before anyone tries to cook it. Fibre is priced at the generous 2 kcal/g; the digestible carbohydrate that carries it in real food costs more on top.

topUps._purpose: What adapt_recipe.py may PROPOSE adding when scaling the dish's own ingredients cannot reach the target. Proposals only — the script prints them with exact grams and never edits a recipe. Adding something to a dish changes the dish, and that is a cooking decision.
topUps._whyCurated: foods.json has cheaper options than these on paper. Flohsamenschalen is 2.5 kcal per gram of fibre and would win every time, but nobody wants psyllium husk stirred into a braise. This list is what actually belongs in a dish, ranked afterwards by cost.
topUps._cuisines: A candidate is offered when the recipe declares no cuisine, or declares one this candidate lists. 'any' fits everything.

fiber.note: holds its shape, better when the dish should stay chunky
carries protein too, so it closes both gaps at once
cheapest in calories, but bulky — wilts into almost anything
very cheap fibre where the dish can take the volume

protein.note: adds protein and almost nothing else; last resort, not a flavour
only where the dish is not heated after adding it

topUps._maxG: Most a serving can sensibly carry of that one thing. Without this the ranking picks whatever is cheapest per gram of fibre and proposes 478 g of spinach — the exact failure inbox/WHAT-TO-LOOK-FOR.md already warns about. When no single candidate fits under its cap, the script proposes a split instead, which is the shape the brief asks for anyway.
